To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
response deprivation is a schedule variable, and that reinforcement is a function of response deprivation.

the rate of a response contingent upon another response can be increased by reducing the rate of that other response, and that this effect is independent of any property of the contingent or instrumental responses.
the effects of reinforcement are due to the effects of response deprivation.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the economic consequences of response deprivation.
the effects of the contingencies under which the organism's behavior is controlled on the properties of its behavior.
the effects of response-depriving schedules on the instrumental performance of pigeons, rats, and monkeys.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
response deprivation, reinforcement, instrumental performance, and economics are all different names for the same thing.
response deprivation is a necessary and sufficient condition for reinforcement of the instrumental response.
reinforcement is a function of response deprivation.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
reinforcement of instrumental behavior is not a property of a response consequence, but a property of a schedule of response consequences.
reinforcement is a special kind of economic transaction.
reinforcement is the product of a special kind of economic transaction.
The main takeaway from our work is that
reinforcement is not an intrinsic property of a response, but rather an emergent property of a response schedule.
response-deprivation schedules, and not reinforcers, are responsible for instrumental reinforcement.

the effects of reinforcement on behavior depend on how the behavior is scheduled and that these effects are not due to special properties of the contingent response but to the economic properties of the schedule.
